title: Anvil per-device security matrix entry
description: One device family per file. The defining virtue of this matrix is honesty: a cell says yes ONLY with an evidence citation, hardware-forbidden cells say 'no' plainly, and anything that could not be confirmed from a public source says 'unverified' with a note describing what would verify it. Every evidence id referenced here must be defined in matrix/evidence/<id>.md.

id.description: Stable family id; must equal the YAML file name without extension.

reference.description: True for reference rows (GrapheneOS-supported Pixels) that define what full support means.

soc.description: System-on-chip capability row. MTE/BTI/PAC here describe the HARDWARE's capability class; whether the vendor actually enables them on this device is documented in mte_notes and limitations.

model.description: SoC model(s); note both variants for dual-chip families.

mte.description: yes = SoC's cores implement ARM MTE (cited); no = cores predate ARMv8.5, so MTE is hardware-forbidden; unverified = capability could not be confirmed from a public source.

bti_pac.description: Hardware coarse-grained CFI (BTI/PAC). partial = mixed-core SoC where only some cores implement it (e.g. big cores yes, Cortex-A55 no).

note.description: Chip-variant split, core generation, and caveats on the capability claims.

bootloader.description: Bootloader unlock/relock story. On most non-Pixel devices both 'officially unlockable' and 'relockable' are gated by vendor policy, not Android.

officially_unlockable.description: Vendor provides a documented, supported unlock path. boolean, or the literal string 'unverified'.

relockable.description: Bootloader can be re-locked after flashing. Note: on most vendors this only works with vendor-signed images, not with a custom OS — that nuance lives in verified_boot.

rollback_protection.description: Bootloader refuses older, more vulnerable firmware/OS (anti-rollback). partial = enforced for some partitions/paths only.

note.description: Unlock mechanics, fuse/warranty consequences, waiting periods, regional restrictions.

verified_boot.description: Android Verified Boot story, focused on the GrapheneOS criterion: can the user run THEIR OWN OS with the bootloader locked and full verified boot?

own_os_with_locked_bl.description: yes = own OS (GrapheneOS) with locked bootloader and full verified boot incl. user-visible key state; partial = relock possible with vendor-signed OS but not demonstrated with a custom OS; no = locked bootloader cannot run a custom OS; unverified = not established.

note.description: Key ownership (vendor vs user keys), yellow/orange boot state behavior, caveats.

attestation.description: Remote attestation row, mirroring GrapheneOS's Auditor/AttestationServer criteria.

hardware.description: Hardware-backed key attestation (TEE or StrongBox). Mandatory for devices launching with Android 8.0+ per CDD/CTS; 'yes' cites that rule plus the launch OS.

strongbox.description: StrongBox keystore provided by a dedicated secure element (true/false), or 'unverified'.

remote_supported_by_grapheneos_auditor.description: Device model is explicitly integrated into GrapheneOS Auditor/AttestationServer (their supported lists are Pixel-only; per-model integration is required).

note.description: Attestation strength caveats (TEE vs StrongBox, softkey-only, remote provisioning).

updates.description: Vendor security-update promise row. ONLY a published vendor commitment goes in the months field; a widely-reported promise you could not reach at review time stays null with the note pointing at the verification path.

vendor_security_period_months.description: Published vendor commitment in months from launch (integer), or null when unverified/EOL.

note.description: What the number means, its source or its verification path, OS-update generations, EOL date if reached.

kernel.description: Kernel situation: GKI version if known, mainline proximity, vendor kernel age.

mte_notes.description: The honest MTE story for this device: capability vs. actual enablement in the shipping OS, and what would verify it.

gsi_feasibility.description: Can a Generic System Image serve as a daily-driver hardened OS? GrapheneOS's own docs reject GSIs outright (kernel changes required); 'good' would require positive evidence for a specific device.

lineage_official.description: Device is on LineageOS's official supported device list (cited), or 'unverified'.

note.description: Official builds, trustworthiness caveats of community builds, GSI caveats.

portable_hardening_score.description: Computed by tools/matrix/matrix_lint.py — redeclared here so files are diff-stable. Weights: MTE 3, relockable own-OS verified boot 3 (partial 1.5), rollback protection 2 (partial 1), hardware attestation 2, vendor security period >= 48 months 1. Maximum 11.

limitations.description: The brutally honest list: hardware-forbidden features, policy walls, unverified areas. Every non-Pixel family must carry at least one entry; entries must state what would verify an 'unverified' area where applicable.

evidence.description: Map of field path or field-group name -> evidence id defined in matrix/evidence/<id>.md. Every non-'no' capability claim MUST carry an evidence entry (exact field path like 'soc.mte', or a group like 'soc'). 'no'/false/null cells may cite evidence too and usually should.

last_reviewed.description: Date of the last human review pass over every cell and citation.
